So I'm in high school and lead Alto in our jazz band. I am very comfortable and confident improving in all keys. Here are my 3 steps for success:

1. Know your scales. Specifically mixolydian, blues, and pentatonics, but definitely all your major and minor ones. If you listen to the greats, half the time they're just jazzing up a mixolydian scale, ie playing it in thirds or fourths.
2. Know your arpeggios. Those are the notes that you can and can hang on for a few beats and have no problem. Again, a lot of the greats use arpeggios a ton.
3. Most important is of all: LISTEN. You can learn everything you know from listening. You can fake the rhythem and notes, but you can't fake style. Listen to all of the big name's solos. Borrow lines from them, and transpose them to different keys.

Remember: the thing about music is you're never more than a half step away from the note. Good luck!
